parts.text: Outline what is meant by a ‘questionnaire’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain one advantage of using a questionnaire rather than an interview in research.

text: Outline what is meant by an ‘aim’. Include an example from one core study from the cognitive
approach in your answer.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by ‘volunteer sampling’, using this study as an example.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Suggest two ways that Milgram could have obtained a volunteer sample with a wider variety
of participants.

text: The study by Milgram (obedience) used volunteer sampling.
In the study by Piliavin et al. (subway Samaritans), participant variables may have affected the
results.
Explain what is meant by ‘participant variables’, using this study as an example.
Dement and Kleitman (sleep and dreams) used a sample of volunteers.
Suggest why this sample may not have been representative of sleep and dreams in the general
population.
Describe the ethical guidelines of ‘numbers’ and ‘replacement’ in relation to animals, using any
examples.
Section B
Answer all questions in this section.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Uma is going to use a structured observation.
Suggest how she could record her data.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Uma cannot decide how many different bird species to observe.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Suggest one reason why it would be better to record a small number of different species.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Suggest one reason why it would be better to record a large number of different species.

text: Uma has a bird feeder in her garden. When she moved the bird feeder, some species of bird
were faster to find it than others. Uma has moved the feeder a second time and is conducting an
observational study to investigate which bird species are faster to learn the new location of the
bird feeder.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by an ‘independent variable’, using Dr Malt’s study as an example.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Suggest how Dr Malt could operationalise her dependent variable.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Explain one advantage of operationalising the dependent variable in this way.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Dr Malt decides she must use deception. She tells the participants in both the ‘new drug
group’ and the ‘old drug group’ that they are receiving the new drug.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Suggest one reason why it is important for Dr Malt to deceive her participants.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Suggest one reason why it is an ethical problem that Dr Malt is deceiving her participants.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text: Suggest how Dr Malt could reduce the problem you have identified in part (c)(ii).

text: Dr Malt is testing whether a new drug to improve attention in mental health patients is better than
an old drug. In her experiment, she is measuring the patients’ attention to a stimulus.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest one way that Zhu could record the number of hours an employee works.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Suggest one way that Zhu could record how happy each employee is.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
For her sample, Zhu is looking for a factory where there is a variety of jobs for the employees.
Suggest two reasons why this is important.

Section C
Answer all questions in this section.

text: Zhu is conducting a correlational study in a factory to investigate the relationship between two
variables:
• the number of hours an employee works
• how happy that employee is.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe how Cari could conduct a field experiment to investigate whether adults who wear
brightly coloured clothing are more helpful than those who do not.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Identify one practical weakness/limitation with the procedure you have described in your
answer to part (a) and suggest how your study might be done differently to overcome the
problem.
Do not refer to ethics or sampling in your answer.

text: Cari thinks that adults wearing brightly coloured clothing are more helpful to children than adults
wearing clothing that is not brightly coloured. She is planning a field experiment to investigate
which adults are more likely to return a ball to children who have kicked it out of reach.
